topic.title: Sample-Efficient Policy Learning and Control
topic.overview: Reinforcement learning must improve a policy from limited interaction while representing values, dynamics, or memory well enough to guide decisions. This cluster brings together model-based policy search, actor–critic methods, approximate policy iteration, and structural conditions for learnability. The focus is on what makes a useful decision representation possible beyond a small tabular environment.
topic.whyItMatters: Large continuous state spaces can hide problems that are statistically impossible without additional structure. Explicit conditions help explain when nonlinear policies or compact recurrent memories can learn efficiently rather than merely succeed on selected benchmarks.
topic.evolution: Early representatives study recurrence detection, control scheduling, and neural sequential decisions. Later work develops data-efficient model-based search and improved critic learning. Recent analyses move beyond linear MDP assumptions and examine low-rank structure, policy generalization, and linear filters that recover useful hidden-state information under specified transition conditions.
openQuestions: Which structural assumptions are testable before expensive interaction?
How can representation guarantees survive imperfect models and changing dynamics?
